target: Every http(s) URL in the repo docs (README, docs/**/*.rst, docs/conf.py, docs/tutorials/*.ipynb, examples/*.py, hypertools/**/*.py, pyproject.toml) manually validated -- 130 unique URLs across 254 files
brainstormed_edge_cases: URL prefixes / f-string fragments extracted as URLs (api.github.com/repos/fivethirtyeight/data/, https://drive, raw .../data/master) must be classified from source context, not naively flagged as 404
Servers that reject HEAD but serve GET (kaggle.com 404-on-HEAD) -- GET fallback required before declaring dead
Bot-blocking hosts (403/999) needing browser User-Agent fallback
Soft-404s: HTTP 200 with 'page not found' body (readthedocs, fivethirtyeight shutdown landing) -- content check needed
#fragment anchors are not validated by HTTP status -- must check id= exists in HTML (sklearn classes.html, matplotlib faq, guides.github.com)
GitHub blob #L<n> line anchors -- pinned file must still have >= n lines (davos#L565, brainiak rsrm.py#L191, ipython #L158/#L3495)
Permanent redirects (301/308) masking moved pages; some redirect INTO a 404 (help.github.com -> docs.github.com)
http:// URLs that should be https:// (brainiak.org, scikit-learn.org, matplotlib.org, readthedocs, wikipedia, jmlr, nips.cc)
Trailing punctuation / markdown-rst closers contaminating extracted URLs -- cross-checked extractor vs raw grep (130==130)
GitHub rate limits: sleep 1.5s between github hits; unauthenticated api.github.com limit 60/hr (only ~5 API hits made)
f-string template URLs with {placeholders} cannot be fetched -- base endpoints validated separately
Endpoint URLs that 400 without query params (docs.google.com/uc?export=download, drive.usercontent.google.com/download) are NOT dead links -- validated via real hypertools.load() download instead
YouTube returns 200 for deleted videos -- must verify via oembed API
Badge URLs (img.shields.io, readthedocs.org/badge) return 200 even when badge says 'not found'/'failing' -- SVG text must be inspected
intersphinx URLs in docs/conf.py -- real validation is fetching <base>/objects.inv, not homepage 200

pip git refs (git+https://github.com/ContextLab/hypertools.git@dev-1.0-refactor) not HTTP-fetchable -- branch existence checked via GitHub API; ALSO tutorials pin a dev branch on the eve of a 1.0 release
DOI redirect chains (dx.doi.org with %2F escaping, doi.org/10.1038/ncomms12141) -- publisher endpoints often block non-browser agents
web.archive.org can exceed 20s timeout -- retries needed before calling it dead
DNS failure (curl exit 6) vs connect timeout (exit 28) -- distinguish dead domain from transient infra
Near-duplicate URLs differing by scheme or trailing slash (http vs https papers.nips.cc, brainiak.org vs brainiak.org/) -- each validated separately
gitter.im room links -- gitter migrated to Matrix; room may 200 but be an empty shell (content check)
GitHub milestone links (milestone/5) can be deleted -> 404

readthedocs /en/latest/ page names from hypertools 0.x (hypertools.tools.reduce.html) may not exist in the 1.0 docs build -- page-level 404 behind project-level 200 (readthedocs 404s often render as 200 fallback pages)
Notebook JSON escaping (\" and \n in source arrays) breaks raw-text regex extraction -- extractor parses JSON cells; verified identical to raw grep
Dataset repos pinned to 'master' branch names (fivethirtyeight/data) -- default-branch rename would silently break raw URLs; verify with real CSV fetch

findings.title: Dead link in plot() docstring: Homebrew install script (master/install -> 404)
findings.description: hypertools/plot/plot.py, in the ffmpeg-install help inside the plot() docstring, tells users to run curl on https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/master/install. Homebrew renamed/moved that file; the path now 404s. Current script is .../Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh (verified 200). The surrounding one-liner is also outdated (uses '/usr/bin/ruby -e', whereas current Homebrew uses '/bin/bash -c ...install.sh').

findings.title: Paper PDF link redirects away to lab homepage (haxbylab HGC+11.pdf)

findings.title: reduce() error-message link points to stale 0.8.1 doc page (and uses http)
findings.description: hypertools/reduce/reduce.py raises ValueError with a message directing users to http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce. Two problems: (1) it uses http:// (301 to https). (2) The page name 'hypertools.tools.reduce' is the OLD 0.8.1 API layout; in the 1.0 codebase this module is hypertools.reduce (docs page hypertools.reduce.html). RTD /en/latest/ currently still serves the 0.8.1 build (browser title: 'hypertools 0.8.1 documentation'), so the link resolves today only by accident; once /latest/ is rebuilt for the 1.0 release the tools.reduce page disappears and this user-facing error link 404s.
findings.repro:
python -c "import hypertools as hy, numpy as np; hy.reduce(np.random.rand(10,5), reduce='NotAModel')"  # message cites .../hypertools.tools.reduce.html
# Evidence: RTD /en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html browser title = 'hypertools 0.8.1 documentation'
findings.expected: https link to the 1.0 reduce docs page (hypertools.reduce.html), stable across the release rebuild.
findings.actual: http link to the 0.8.1-only page name hypertools.tools.reduce.html; will 404 after /latest/ rebuilds for 1.0.

In current scikit-learn (1.9), classes.html JS-redirects to /api/index.html and the redirect drops the fragment; the #module-sklearn.decomposition anchor does not exist on the landing page (the API reference was reorganized into per-module pages like /api/sklearn.decomposition.html). findings.title: Numerous http:// doc links 301-redirect to https:// (should use https)
findings.description: Many documented links use http:// and 301-redirect to https://: README.md (scikit-learn.org, matplotlib.org, hypertools.readthedocs.io x2, and web.archive/jmlr as http natives), hypertools/align/procrustes.py (en.wikipedia.org x2, dx.doi.org), hypertools/tools/align.py + external/brainiak.py (brainiak.org, papers.nips.cc, apache.org), hypertools/reduce/reduce.py (readthedocs), and tutorial markdown (matplotlib.org, scikit-learn.org, papers.nips.cc, brainiak.org). All resolve via redirect but should be https for a 1.0 release. EXCLUDE http://www.w3.org/2000/svg and http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink in _shared/animated_svg.py -- those are XML namespace literals and MUST remain http per the SVG spec.
findings.repro: for u in http://scikit-learn.org/ http://matplotlib.org/ http://brainiak.org http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procrustes_transformation; do curl -sIL --max-time 20 $u -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n'; done  # each 301 -> https
findings.expected: https:// scheme for external documentation links.
findings.actual: http:// with 301 redirect to https:// (e.g. http://brainiak.org -> https://brainiak.org/).

findings.title: Outdated GitHub repo link: IntelPNI/brainiak (moved to brainiak/brainiak)
findings.description: hypertools/tools/align.py links https://github.com/IntelPNI/brainiak, which 301-redirects to https://github.com/brainiak/brainiak (the project moved orgs). findings.title: Legacy dx.doi.org resolver with %2F-encoded slash in procrustes.py
findings.description: hypertools/align/procrustes.py cites http://dx.doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02289451. It resolves (via a 301/302 chain to the Cambridge/Psychometrika article) but uses the legacy dx.doi.org resolver and an unusual %2F-encoded path slash. Canonical form is https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02289451.
findings.repro: curl -sIL --max-time 20 http://dx.doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02289451 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n'  # resolves via redirects to cambridge.org

findings.title: All tutorials + docs/conf.py pip-install hypertools from the dev-1.0-refactor branch
findings.description: 13 tutorial notebooks (align, analyze, cluster, conversation_trajectories, hugging_face_embeddings, lsl_streaming, modern_sklearn_dynamics, normalize, plot, reduce, streaming_data, text, wikipedia_embeddings) and the sphinx-gallery install cell in docs/conf.py install via 'git+https://github.com/ContextLab/hypertools.git@dev-1.0-refactor'. The branch exists today (GitHub API 200), so notebooks run now, but for a 1.0 release these should pin '@v1.0.0' (or install the released 'hypertools' from PyPI). As written, a scientist running a published tutorial after release silently gets the moving dev branch rather than the 1.0 release, and the pin will eventually break when the branch is deleted/merged.
findings.repro:
grep -rl 'hypertools.git@dev-1.0-refactor' docs/tutorials/*.ipynb docs/conf.py | wc -l  # 14 files
curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/ContextLab/hypertools/branches/dev-1.0-refactor | python -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["name"])'  # dev-1.0-refactor (exists now)
findings.expected: Tutorials/docs pin the released version (@v1.0.0) or install from PyPI for a 1.0 release.
findings.actual: All install from the mutable dev-1.0-refactor branch.
